definition: A way to speed up text generation: a small, fast model drafts the next few tokens and the large model checks them all in one pass, keeping the ones it agrees with.
eli5: A quick helper guesses the next few words and the expert only says yes or no, which is faster than the expert writing every word.

definition: A model built to choose from a fixed set of options and return a calibrated probability for each, instead of writing free text. Used for routing, classification and grading inside apps and agents.
eli5: Instead of writing an essay, it ticks one box on a multiple-choice sheet and says how sure it is.

definition: A setting that tells a model how much thinking to spend on a request, so you can trade cost and speed against answer quality task by task.
eli5: Like choosing whether to answer a quiz quickly or take your time and check your work.

definition: AI that senses and acts in the physical world, such as robots, drones and self-driving systems, rather than only working with text and images on a screen.
eli5: AI with a body: it can look around a room and move things in it, not just chat.

definition: The ability of an assistant or agent to keep facts from earlier conversations and use them later, instead of starting fresh in every session.
eli5: Like a friend who remembers your name and what you talked about last week.

definition: An isolated environment where an AI agent can run code and use tools without being able to touch the rest of the computer or network. Microsoft's Execution Containers (MXC) are one example.
eli5: A sandpit with walls: the agent can build and break things inside it, but nothing outside gets hurt.

definition: A way for authorised people to pause or shut down an AI system, even in the middle of a task, if it behaves in ways it should not.
eli5: A big red stop button for the AI.

definition: An attention pattern where each token looks only at a fixed number of nearby tokens instead of the whole input, so memory and compute stay flat as the text gets longer.
eli5: Reading a long book while keeping only the last few pages open in front of you.

definition: Removing the weights or parts of a model that matter least, so it runs faster and uses less memory with little loss in quality.
eli5: Trimming the branches of a plant that bear no fruit so the rest grows better.

definition: Designing a whole data-centre rack, with its chips, networking, power and cooling, as one system so many GPUs work together like a single large computer.
eli5: Building the whole cupboard of computers as one machine instead of buying the parts one by one.

definition: One of the few companies that run cloud data centres at enormous scale, such as Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, and supply most of the computing power used to train and run AI.
eli5: The giant landlords who own the buildings full of computers that AI runs on.
